sci-repo-y10-sby-2017-s1exam-mc-1.title: Year 10 Science — Semester1 two-hour exam — SafetyBay2017 (original source MC)
sci-repo-y10-sby-2017-s1exam-mc-1.coverage: Original assessment questions with source figures. Written parts remain in the bank with marks and parent context. Review-required items excluded from automatic battles.

questions.prompt: Chromosomes are found in the nucleus of:
options: stem cells that have not yet differentiated
questions.explanation: Most nucleated body cells contain chromosomes; mature red blood cells are an exception.

questions.prompt: The periodic table:
options: is a systematic chart listing all known elements
arranges elements from lowest to highest atomic number
arranges elements in columns called groups
questions.explanation: All three describe the periodic table.

questions.prompt: What is the term used for a row in the periodic table?
questions.explanation: A row is a period.

questions.prompt: If a disease in humans is said to be sex linked, what pair of chromosomes must contain the gene responsible for the disease?
questions.explanation: Sex chromosomes are conventionally the23rd pair in a human karyotype; sex linkage refers to loci onX orY.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a noble (inert) gas?
questions.explanation: Neon is a noble gas.

questions.prompt: If a diploid cell in a plant has 32 chromosomes, how many chromosomes will be in each gamete?
questions.explanation: Gametes have half the diploid number:16.

questions.prompt: Which group number do the alkaline earth metals belong to?
questions.explanation: Alkaline earth metals are group2.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is the most reactive metal element?
questions.explanation: Potassium is the most reactive listed metal under the intended comparison; steel is an alloy.

questions.prompt: Which of the following best describes what occurs during anaphase?
options: Chromosomes line up in a single line across the centre of the cell
Chromosomes become visible and the nuclear membrane disappears
Chromatids are pulled apart by spindle fibers, toward the poles of the cell
Cytoplasm divides down the middle of the cell
questions.explanation: During mitotic anaphase sister chromatids separate toward opposite poles.

questions.prompt: The structure of DNA may be described as a twisted ladder. Recall what forms the upright parts of the ladder.
questions.explanation: Alternating sugar and phosphate form the DNA backbone.

questions.prompt: During which phase does the DNA condense into chromosomes?
questions.explanation: Prophase involves chromosome condensation. DNA is present throughout the cycle, not created at prophase.

questions.prompt: How many daughter cells are produced in meiosis?
questions.explanation: Typically four haploid cells.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of metals?
questions.explanation: Brittleness is not a typical general property of metals; many metals are malleable/ductile.

questions.prompt: The elements that sit between group 3 and 12 of the periodic table are known as the:
questions.explanation: The centrald-block corresponds broadly to transition metals;group12 classification has technical exceptions.

questions.prompt: An allele is best defined as
options: a type of gene found only on the sex chromosome
an alternative form of gene at a given position on the chromosome.
questions.explanation: An allele is an alternative form/sequence of a gene at a locus.

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements about atoms is true?
options: Neutrons and protons are found in the nucleus with the electrons
The number of neutrons found in the nucleus of an atom is always the same
Protons circle the nucleus all the time
An atom is mostly empty space
questions.explanation: An atom is mostly empty space in the elementary nuclear model.

questions.prompt: The nucleus of an atom is made up of
questions.explanation: Nuclei contain protons and usually neutrons;hydrogen-1 has none.

questions.prompt: An ion is best defined as: An atom which has
questions.explanation: A monatomic ion has lost or gained electrons and has net charge. Polyatomic ions also exist.

questions.prompt:
The atomic symbol for a gold atom is . Clarify what this tells you about the gold atom.
[LV-MEDIA:{"images":[{"pack":"repo-science-batch15","id":"e32-image3"}]}]
options: It contains a total of 197 protons, neutrons and electrons.
questions.explanation: ¹⁹⁷₇₉Au has197−79=118 neutrons.

questions.prompt: What is the electronic configuration of a chlorine atom? Hint: Chlorine has an atomic number of 17?
questions.explanation: Neutral chlorine:2,8,7.

questions.prompt: A phosphorus atom has an atomic number of 15. State how many electrons it has in its third (outermost) shell.
questions.explanation: Neutral phosphorus:2,8,5,so five outer-shell electrons.

questions.prompt: A radionuclide is:
options: an element that emits beta radiation.
an atom with the same number of protons but a different number of neutrons.
questions.explanation: A radionuclide is a radioactive nuclide/isotope.

questions.prompt: The mass number of an atom is the number of
options: protons plus neutrons in the nucleus.
questions.explanation: Mass number is protons plus neutrons.

questions.prompt: Which of the following will cause an atom to become a negative ion?
questions.explanation: Gaining electrons produces a negative ion without changing the element’s proton number.

questions.prompt:
Scientists use the process of decay in radioactive isotopes called  to determine the  of organisms.
[LV-MEDIA:{"images":[{"pack":"repo-science-batch15","id":"e32-image4"}]}]
questions.explanation: Carbon dating uses radioactivecarbon decay to estimate time since carbon exchange ceased,within its useful range;not all isotopic dating is carbon dating.

questions.prompt: State the general name for organisms that cause disease.
questions.explanation: Pathogen is the general term.

questions.prompt: Identify the chemicals or drugs that kill bacteria
questions.explanation: Antibiotics act against susceptible bacteria;some inhibit growth rather than directly killing.

questions.prompt:
Four paper discs were soaked in antibiotics. The discs were placed on a plate with a large number of colonies of bacteria. The aim of the experiment was to test the effectiveness of the antibiotics. After three days the plate was examined. The results are shown above. Identify the antibiotic that was most effective in killing the bacteria. The one in disk
[LV-MEDIA:{"images":[{"pack":"repo-science-batch15","id":"e32-image5"}]}]
questions.explanation: DiscC has the largest clear inhibition zone in the supplied diagram. Valid comparison assumes equal discs/concentrations and suitable controls;zone diameter is not a universal direct measure of drug potency.

questions.prompt: Which of these will be in the first line of defence?
questions.explanation: Skin is a first-line barrier.

questions.prompt: The products of the body’s endocrine system are
questions.explanation: Endocrine glands secrete hormones.

questions.prompt: An island chain such as the Hawaiian Islands, provided evidence for which tectonic process?
questions.explanation: A. The Hawaiian chain records plate motion over a hotspot,not a subduction island arc.

questions.prompt: When was the supercontinent, Pangea, formed on the surface of the Earth?
questions.explanation: D is the source’s nearest interval,though assembly began earlier and timing depends on what stage ofPangaea is meant.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is the correct order of the layers of the Earth, from the centre to the surface?
options: Crust, Mantle, Outer Core, Inner Core
Inner Core, Outer Core, Mantle, Crust
Outer Core, Inner Core, Mantle, Crust
Mantle, Inner Core, Crust, Outer Core
questions.explanation: Inner core→outer core→mantle→crust.
